lead.headline: G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil to curb diesel prices
lead.dek: Four-month drawdown through the International Energy Agency begins at once, with a diesel release front-loaded into the first 20 days
body: The Group of Seven agreed Friday to release 100 million barrels of oil through the International Energy Agency over four months, beginning immediately and front-loading a diesel release into the first 20 days, after an emergency video conference called by French President Emmanuel Macron, the group's chair.

The G7 statement said members would also refrain from energy export restrictions among themselves and coordinate refinery maintenance so plants do not shut at once, CBS News and Euronews reported. The call followed an overnight Trump-Macron conversation; Trump had threatened a U.S. diesel export ban and said afterward that "what Europe did was a great thing." Spread evenly, the release is about 830,000 barrels a day, Euronews said.

U.S. diesel averaged $6.37 a gallon Friday, up about 70% since late February, and Brent crude closed at $102.25, NBC News reported; the record diesel price was $6.52 on Sept. 22. Andy Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates told NBC a release of this size could cut diesel by about 25 cents a gallon temporarily. The IEA released 400 million barrels in March, about two-thirds of it delivered, Al Jazeera said.

briefs.headline: Employers add 29,000 jobs in September as unemployment hits 4.2%
briefs.summary: Payrolls grew by 29,000, against a 90,000 forecast, and July and August were revised down a combined 60,000, the Labor Department said Friday. Wages rose 3.0% on the year, the smallest gain since May 2021.

briefs.headline: GOP Senate super PAC pulls North Carolina ads, shifts to Kansas
briefs.summary: Senate Leadership Fund canceled its airtime for Michael Whatley against Roy Cooper and reserved more than $8 million in Kansas, where Sen. Roger Marshall faces Democrat Adam Hamilton, NBC News reported Friday.

briefs.headline: Judge rules federal ban on noncitizen voting unconstitutional
briefs.summary: U.S. District Judge David Leibowitz in Florida dismissed a charge against a Jamaican national over a 2020 vote, ruling Thursday that only states set voter qualifications, CBS News reported. The Justice Department appealed.

briefs.headline: U.S. measles count reaches 3,886 as Pennsylvania passes 970 cases
briefs.summary: The CDC added 228 cases in Friday's weekly update, an eighth straight triple-digit week, across 42 outbreaks. Pennsylvania reported 977 cases, most of any state, and a fifth death.

briefs.headline: Two tankers struck near Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
briefs.summary: UK Maritime Trade Operations said unidentified projectiles hit two oil tankers in separate incidents, one four nautical miles east of Oman, with crews safe. Hormuz traffic is about 75% below pre-conflict levels, it said.

briefs.headline: U.S. suspends consular services in Brazil two days before vote
briefs.summary: The embassy cited unspecified security concerns Friday and Australia closed its embassy too. Federal police searched sites in Sao Paulo and Brasilia but said they found no evidence of a threat. Brazil votes Sunday.

briefs.headline: North Korea fires ballistic missile more than 700 km into sea
briefs.summary: South Korea's military said the missile launched from Wonsan on Saturday; Japan's Defense Ministry put the range at about 680 km. It came a day after Pyongyang dismissed Seoul's demand for an apology over DMZ mine blasts.

briefs.headline: Latvia votes with Russia and living costs on the ballot
briefs.summary: About 1.5 million voters choose a 100-seat Saeima contested by 14 parties Saturday, with four German Eurofighters patrolling at Riga's request, DW said. Partial results are due in the evening.

briefs.headline: HEPC keeps Salem University out of state aid another year
briefs.summary: The commission voted Friday to continue the suspension, citing continued eligibility and disbursement problems; 135 students are affected and Salem may reapply next June.

briefs.headline: Morrisey office reviews options as Ohio suspends its gas tax
briefs.summary: Ohio's 38.5-cent tax is suspended for 90 days from Sunday. A Morrisey spokesperson told WSAZ on Friday the office is "closely reviewing options"; West Virginia's tax is 35.7 cents a gallon.

briefs.headline: PSC lets West Virginia American Water run Kanawha Falls PSD now
briefs.summary: Commissioners approved an interim agreement Friday letting the company operate the Fayette County district immediately, ahead of a sale of three PSDs for about $13 million, WVVA reported.

briefs.headline: Huntington picked for $96M federal homelessness treatment program
briefs.summary: HHS named Huntington one of eight communities in its new STREETS program Friday; each gets $3 million a year for four years for outreach, treatment and housing for people with mental illness or addiction.

regional.item: Cabell County commissioners named Grace Taylor interim county clerk Thursday after Scott Caserta's retirement.
BridgeValley's president told its board Friday he is unsure Montgomery's Davis Hall is viable after June flooding hit five of six floors.
A car hit a utility pole on Gihon Road at 2:34 p.m. Friday, closing the road and rerouting two Wood County school buses, WTAP said.
Hinton's 60th Railroad Days runs Oct. 9-11 with free city parking and a downtown Route 64 closure, the city manager told WVVA on Thursday.

away.item: U.S. 7 between Bennington's Exit 2 and Arlington's Exit 3 reopened to two-way traffic Thursday at 5 p.m., ahead of schedule.

hotspots.item: Supporters of Garage Strong, a youth gym in Addison's former Dollar General building, filled a Sept. 22 town commission meeting on its future, the Echo said Tuesday.
The Topsail Nature Preserve, its beaches and its parking lot close the morning of Oct. 7 for herbicide treatment of invasive common reed, WWAY reported Friday.

briefs.headline: Howe Sound mill rescue renews debate over Northwood closure
briefs.summary: A deal keeping Domtar's 400-worker Howe Sound mill open drew questions in Prince George about why Canfor's Northwood, about 300 jobs, got no such help; Canfor says Northwood has lost about $460 million since 2018.

briefs.headline: Giddens launches re-election bid in Prince George-Mackenzie
briefs.summary: The Conservative MLA said resource jobs and northern cardiac care will anchor his campaign; as of Thursday afternoon no rival had filed in the riding, CKPG reported. Nominations closed Saturday.

briefs.headline: Doerkson pledges water bomber fleet as Eby vows grocery price caps
briefs.summary: Conservative interim leader Lorne Doerkson promised about $500 million for a Crown-owned water bomber fleet in Summerland on Friday; Eby in Kelowna pledged margin ceilings on six staples, The Canadian Press said.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CKPG Today

briefs.headline: Five foreign nationals charged in B.C. extortion and arson probe
briefs.summary: Langley RCMP said four men were arrested in Surrey on Thursday and one at Toronto Pearson in a case that began with a June 2025 auto dealer extortion and led to arsons and shootings.

briefs.headline: Rivals target PQ referendum plan as Quebec vote nears Monday
briefs.summary: CAQ Leader Christine Frechette warned of "colossal damage" and Conservative Eric Duhaime staged 1995 Yes and No buses Friday, while Paul St-Pierre Plamondon called it fearmongering, The Canadian Press reported.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CTV News

briefs.headline: Liberal MP Zahid says violent rhetoric puts all MPs at risk
briefs.summary: Salma Zahid has had round-the-clock security since five cars were torched outside her Scarborough home in August, and said language aimed at NDP Leader Avi Lewis endangers him, The Canadian Press reported.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CKPG Today

briefs.headline: Fossil study pushes animal origins back 200 million years
briefs.summary: An Oxford-led team says Mongolia's Kheseen Biota undercuts the case for a 590-million-year origin and puts the first animals at 700 million to 800 million years ago, in Science Advances.

briefs.headline: Crew-12 to undock Monday after Sunday handover on station
briefs.summary: NASA said Jessica Meir's crew targets an early Oct. 5 departure, weather permitting, for a splashdown off California; a change-of-command ceremony is set for 10:20 a.m. ET Sunday with 11 people aboard.

briefs.headline: Type I superconductor found to break time-reversal symmetry
briefs.summary: IISER Bhopal researchers cooled ytterbium antimonide crystals and used muons to detect spontaneous internal magnetic fields, a first for a type I material, in Physical Review Letters.

briefs.headline: Congo Ebola deaths pass 4,000 as unpaid workers protest
briefs.summary: Congo's health ministry counted 4,018 deaths among 8,300 confirmed cases Thursday; surveillance workers protested unpaid wages in Bunia and an infected MSF worker was flown to the Netherlands.

briefs.headline: Apple tightens Mac disk access over AI agent risks
briefs.summary: Apple said Friday some developers use Full Disk Access in ways that expose everything on a system, and new macOS controls will require more explicit user action, TechCrunch reported.

briefs.headline: FAA's AI air traffic tool draws scrutiny after D.C. rollout
briefs.summary: The SMART tool, combining 200 data streams, has run since Sept. 21 for Reagan, Dulles and BWI traffic; Rep. Don Beyer said FAA chief Bryan Bedford eased his concerns, Nextgov reported.

briefs.headline: AI models top CPAs on bookkeeping benchmark, Mercor says
briefs.summary: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 scored 61.8% on Mercor's 160-task APEX accounting test against about 37% for 12 licensed CPAs, the vendor said, though no model fully solved 58% of tasks.

weather_ear: Saturday's forecast follows from Jim Claudtore at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster ran no regional line; Latvia votes today, Brazil on Sunday, and the Division Series open this afternoon.
